name: Heavy-rain and urban flooding – Montréal region
description: Remnants of tropical storm Debby dropped 154 mm at Montréal–Trudeau airport on 9 August 2024, a daily record (221 mm at Lanoraie), flooding basements and roads.

documented_events: August 2024: 154 mm in a day at YUL (ECCC 2024)
July 2023: record wet July in Quebec (ECCC 2023 list)
practical_implications: Basement backflow and overland flooding; check municipal flood maps

sources.title: Canada's 10 most impactful weather stories of 2024
Canada's Changing Climate Report (2019) – Headline statements
sources.publisher: Government of Canada (Environment and Climate Change Canada, lead)
sources.methodology: Assessment report; statements are assessments of observed and projected change, not local forecasts

verification.notes: Event facts quoted or paraphrased from the cited official pages on 2026-10-30. Exposure and implications are agent-04 interpretation.

limitations: Spring river flooding (Ottawa River, Rivière des Prairies) not documented here. Past events show exposure; they are not a prediction for any particular year. Exposure varies street by street – check municipal and provincial hazard maps for a specific property.
